reviewStatus: Drafted from verified sources; pending independent clinician review before clinical release.
commonErrors: Mixing modified and unmodified use without stating which.
name: Hunt and Hess Scale

version.label: Hunt & Hess 1968 (original, with modifier)
version.detail: Serious systemic disease or severe arteriographic vasospasm moves the grade one level worse (maximum V). Many units omit the modifier; this implementation applies it only when selected.

purpose: Clinical grading of aneurysmal subarachnoid haemorrhage.

options.label: Asymptomatic, or minimal headache and slight neck stiffness
Moderate to severe headache, neck stiffness; no deficit other than cranial nerve palsy
Drowsiness, confusion, or mild focal deficit
Stupor, moderate to severe hemiparesis; possible early decerebrate rigidity
Deep coma, decerebrate rigidity, moribund appearance

inputDefinitions.label: Serious systemic disease or severe arteriographic vasospasm
inputDefinitions.help: Original examples: hypertension, diabetes, severe arteriosclerosis, chronic pulmonary disease.

resultStates.label: Grade II
resultStates.summary: Headache and meningism without focal deficit (cranial nerve palsy allowed).

resultStates.label: Grade III
resultStates.summary: Drowsiness, confusion or mild focal deficit.

resultStates.label: Grade IV
resultStates.detail: Assess for hydrocephalus, seizures and other reversible causes according to local protocol.

resultStates.label: Grade V
resultStates.detail: Assess for hydrocephalus, seizures and other reversible causes according to local protocol.

clinicalContext.text: A long-standing clinical grading scale for aneurysmal SAH.

clinicalInsights.text: The grade includes the original systemic disease/vasospasm modifier; state this when reporting.
Grade can change after treatment of hydrocephalus or seizures; record timing.

limitations: The modifier is applied inconsistently between centres.
whatItDoesNotTellYou: Vasospasm or delayed cerebral ischaemia risk.

guideSections.what: A five-grade clinical classification of aneurysmal SAH.
guideSections.howToPerform: Choose the best-fitting description; apply the modifier only if using the original version.
guideSections.clinicalContext: Grades IV–V are commonly termed poor grade.

sources.citation: Hunt WE, Hess RM. Surgical risk as related to time of intervention in the repair of intracranial aneurysms. J Neurosurg. 1968;28(1):14-20.

components.label: Serious systemic disease or severe arteriographic vasospasm
